headline: 17 police injured as garment workers clash with police in Uttara
summary: Protesters demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000 and payment of arrears clashed with law enforcers in Dhaka.
details: Garment workers in Dhaka’s Uttara area clashed with police today while demonstrating for a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000 and the payment of arrears.
At least 17 police personnel were injured during the clash, including an Industrial Police constable who suffered a broken hand.
A police pickup van and a motorcycle were vandalised as protesters reportedly hurled brickbats at law enforcers.
The clash was triggered when workers attempted to block the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in the Rajlakshmi area around 10:30 am.
Rezaul Karim, deputy commissioner of the DMP’s Uttara Division, stated that police initially tried to persuade the demonstrators to leave the road before they became agitated.
Police responded by using sound grenades and water cannons to disperse the crowd, leading to a chase and counter-chase that lasted nearly an hour.
As of late afternoon, it had not been confirmed whether any garment workers were injured during the confrontation.
caption:
17 police officers injured and vehicles vandalised in Uttara as garment workers protest for higher wages.

Garment workers in Dhaka’s Uttara area clashed with police today while demonstrating for a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000 and the payment of arrears.

A police pickup van and a motorcycle were vandalised as protesters reportedly hurled brickbats at law enforcers.

The clash was triggered when workers attempted to block the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in the Rajlakshmi area around 10:30 am.

Rezaul Karim, deputy commissioner of the DMP’s Uttara Division, stated that police initially tried to persuade the demonstrators to leave the road before they became agitated.

Police responded by using sound grenades and water cannons to disperse the crowd, leading to a chase and counter-chase that lasted nearly an hour.

As of late afternoon, it had not been confirmed whether any garment workers were injured during the confrontation.

headline: Doctor suspended after PM catches him smoking at children's hospital
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman ordered the suspension of Dr Rafiqul Islam during a surprise inspection of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute.
details: A doctor at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute has been suspended after Prime Minister Tarique Rahman found him smoking in his office during a surprise inspection on Saturday.
The prime minister expressed strong dissatisfaction after finding the doctor smoking and noting that the office room was untidy.
Following the prime minister's instructions, the hospital's governing board chairman, Prof AKM Azizul Haque, took immediate action, leading to the suspension of Dr Rafiqul Islam.
The visit was part of a day-long tour of hospitals and educational institutions in Dhaka to assess cleanliness and dengue prevention measures.
During the inspection, the prime minister urged doctors and staff to maintain hygiene and carry out their professional duties with responsibility.
Earlier that day, the prime minister also visited the Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital in Uttara, where he expressed dissatisfaction with the management.
caption:
A surprise visit by the Prime Minister leads to an immediate suspension. A doctor was caught smoking in his office at a children's hospital.

A doctor at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute has been suspended after Prime Minister Tarique Rahman found him smoking in his office during a surprise inspection on Saturday.

The prime minister expressed strong dissatisfaction after finding the doctor smoking and noting that the office room was untidy.

Following the prime minister's instructions, the hospital's governing board chairman, Prof AKM Azizul Haque, took immediate action, leading to the suspension of Dr Rafiqul Islam.

The visit was part of a day-long tour of hospitals and educational institutions in Dhaka to assess cleanliness and dengue prevention measures.

During the inspection, the prime minister urged doctors and staff to maintain hygiene and carry out their professional duties with responsibility.

Earlier that day, the prime minister also visited the Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital in Uttara, where he expressed dissatisfaction with the management.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #HealthCare #Accountability #News

Source: Jamuna TV, bdnews24.com, Prothom Alo
